lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Susan, it's Rachel from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, rough week. My feet are numb again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 1.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just get out there, even when it's hot.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: This heat is killing me. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd be out there if you could find a time of day that doesn't feel like an oven.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to walk 15 minutes on 4 days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 4.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If finding the time gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 1 out of 4 days, the hard part was the rain, and next week you're going to walk 15 minutes on 4 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Susan. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Check-in on wellbeing, but no follow-up on feelings
Reports numb feet again; not followed up
Fatigue cited as reason not to walk
Heat named as barrier; spouse change
Reflects desire to walk despite heat
Summary misstates barrier as rain, not heat
Sets midweek text and next call

flags.reason: Persistent numb feet (possible treatment neuropathy) acknowledged with 'Got it' and not explored; fall risk not assessed.
Directive advice pushed after participant's sustain talk about heat, without asking permission.
'You need to walk every day, no excuses' argues against fatigue and shames rather than evoking change.
Goal of 15 minutes on 4 days was set unilaterally rather than collaboratively; confidence only 4/10.
Summary says the hard part was rain; participant named heat and time of day as barriers.

score.summary: The coach used some good moves, such as asking permission before offering the mall idea and eliciting a backup plan, and Susan responded with several change statements. However, the coach repeatedly persuaded ('no excuses', 'I want you to walk 15 minutes on 4 days') and let the numb feet report pass without follow-up.
strengths: Line 11: asked permission before offering suggestions.
Line 21: complex reflection named Susan's ambivalence and validated it.
Line 38: open question elicited a backup plan that drew change talk (line 39).
Line 40: closed the call with a summary and clear next contact (line 42).
coaching_tips: Line 17: replace 'no excuses' with an open question about what would make daily walking feasible given her fatigue.
Line 34: offer the 15-minute goal as an option, e.g., 'What feels like a realistic next step for you?'
Line 4: briefly ask about the numbness and whether she has had a fall or trouble with balance, and suggest raising it with her care team.
Line 40: correct the barrier summary to heat and time of day, using her own words.
